external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A member of the grocery loyalty programme.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop and spend them on gift cards.
external_entities.notes: Member sign-in and approval behaviour is described, but the member's operating environment is not placed in a trust zone.

external_entities.name: partner app
external_entities.description: A web application operated by another company, such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers
external_entities.notes: The partner app is an external system because another company runs it.

external_entities.name: browser
external_entities.description: A member's browser used to sign in and approve a partner-app connection.
external_entities.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser
external_entities.notes: The text does not state where the browser runs.

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application used by members to sign in and call the rewards API.
processes.notes: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone. Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The server that authenticates members, handles authorization-code flows, issues tokens and manages partner consents.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
processes.notes: The member's sign-in is kept in a cookie for thirty days; nobody decided an idle timeout for it.

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The API that reads and writes the points ledger and receives requests from the mobile app and partner apps.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
processes.notes: Access tokens are bearer JWTs. The API checks the signature with a public key downloaded at startup, but does not check the client or audience.

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.
processes.notes: The console uses access tokens from the same authorization server and is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

processes.name: partnerships team
processes.description: The team that registers partner apps and grants them client credentials and scopes.
processes.source_excerpt: Our partnerships team registers each partner app by hand
processes.notes: The text names the team as an actor performing registration, but does not describe its interface or operating environment.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: The database containing member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_stores.notes: Refresh tokens remain in the database after an account is closed.

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: The ledger holding every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction
data_stores.notes: The ledger records which client made each change, but not which member approved it.

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: The store receiving every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: use app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.data_description: rewards requests and member points data

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The browser submits the member's sign-in interaction to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser
data_flows.notes: The member's sign-in is kept in a cookie for thirty days.
data_flows.data_description: member sign-in credentials and session cookie

data_flows.name: approve consent
data_flows.description: The browser submits the member's approval of the listed scopes to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: approves a consent screen that lists the scopes

data_flows.name: return code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.notes: An authorization code stays valid for ten minutes.

data_flows.name: request tokens
data_flows.description: The partner app sends its client secret in the body of token requests to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.notes: Partner apps receive every scope. Redirect URI matching accepts any URI that starts with the registered URI.
data_flows.data_description: client ID, client secret and authorization code

data_flows.name: read points
data_flows.description: A partner app calls the rewards API to show a member's points.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a meal-planning service that shows a member's points

data_flows.name: manage identities
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores and manages member identities, authorization artifacts and consents in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_flows.notes: This also includes authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.
data_flows.data_description: member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents

data_flows.name: update ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, including balances and transactions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

data_flows.name: write logs
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes every received request, including headers, to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store

data_flows.name: take tokens
data_flows.description: The support console takes access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.
data_flows.notes: Closing an account does not affect that member's refresh tokens.
